A_target.statement:
Let $x \in \R$ with $x > -1$, and let $r \ge 1$.
Then:
:$\paren {1 + x}^r \ge 1 + r x$

B_source.statement:
Let $f$ be a [[Definition:Convex Real Function|convex]] [[Definition:Differentiable Real Function|differentiable]] function on an [[Definition:Open Real Interval|open interval]] $I$.
Let $x_0 \in I$.
Then:
:$\forall x \in I: \map f x \ge \map f {x_0} + \map {f'} {x_0} \paren {x - x_0}$

validity_conditions: The tangent line at x0 = 0 is f(0) + f'(0)x = 1 + rx.
Convexity puts the graph above this tangent, giving Bernoulli's inequality.
proof_plan:
Let $\map f x = \paren {1 + x}^r$ on $\openint {-1} \infty$.
As $\map {f''} x = r \paren {r - 1} \paren {1 + x}^{r - 2} \ge 0$ for $r \ge 1$, $f$ is [[Definition:Convex Real Function|convex]].

Take $x_0 = 0$ in the tangent line inequality:
:$\map f x \ge \map f 0 + \map {f'} 0 x$
